messages:
maya: quick heads-up — canary rollout of nf4+fp4 mix (route selector v2) in us-west triggered a sustained 20-30% throughput tail for ~10m and a transient node-level RSS spike (~6GB) on a few hosts. logs attached in thread.
eli: saw that in CI too, noticed spike when mixed-batch traffic hit >2 concurrent streams per worker. looks like a scheduler path picked two different 4-bit kernels and forced a host-copy for KV fallback.
sam: any flamegraphs/prof? can we repro locally with perf/pprof?
maya: repro steps below, cheap repro using loadgen with mixed batch sizes 1/8/32 hitting the canary model. profiling shows a hot memcpy path in "kv_merge_copyback".

```
# repro
./tools/loadgen --model redwood/nf4-canary --mix "1:50,8:30,32:20" --concurrency 16 --region us-west
perf record -g -p <pid>
pprof -http=:6060 /tmp/profile.pb
```

eli: here's an excerpt of the pprof flame graph (top stack):
- schedule_kernel_selector
- choose_quant_variant
- prepare_kv_checkpoint
- kv_merge_copyback (heavy)
- cudaMemcpy (host->device)
- kernel_dispatch

anya: that host memcpy is the smoking gun — we accidentally chose a kernel variant that doesn't support on-device KV layout for packetized batches, so we fallback to host staging.
sam: why did selector pick that variant? heuristics should prefer on-device-compatible kernels for small latency-sensitive batches.
maya: selector v2 changed tie-break to prefer "latency_estimate" over "kv_compatibility" for mixed precision. that helped avg latency in other traffic shapes but exposed this head-of-line case.
tomas: perf-bot shows this path only when packing ratio > 0.6 and when sequence_len_distribution median > 512. we need a conditional rule.

perf-bot: incident-note: 2310056789 — canary nf4-fp4 selector-v2 -> throughput tail and RSS spike observed on 3 hosts (us-west). Auto-rollback not triggered.

eli: quick mitigation options:
1) revert selector v2
2) add a hard gate in selector: if packing_ratio > 0.5 prefer kv_compatible kernels
3) patch kernel metadata so selector knows which kernel supports in-place KV

anya: prefer (2) + (3). revert is disruptive for other regions.
sam: agree. (2) is low-risk. I can raise a PR to change the tie-break ordering and add telemetry flags.

maya: adding additional telemetry fields that record chosen_kernel_id + kv_layout_flag will let us monitor without a revert. can we add a sampler (1%) first?

tomas: I'll roll a 1% sampler for chosen_kernel telemetry and pack_ratio tag. also will add an alert rule if per-host memcpy time > 15% of CPU time for 5m.

sam: PR #4521 created: selector: prefer_kv_compatible_when_packing_high. patch includes unit tests and a small migration for saved heuristics.

maya: test plan: canary 5% -> monitor sampler metrics for 30m -> promote if no memcpy spikes. if spike reappears, autoscale down canary and rollback.

eli: also add a quick kernel metadata check during model-attach so we fail fast if kernel doesn't declare kv in-place support.

anya: filed ticket infra-2047 for kernel metadata enforcement.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary-changeset-4521 -> us-west (5% traffic). started at 2026-03-18T15:07:00Z

maya: thanks everyone. follow-ups: sam to finish PR tests, tomas to enable telemetry sampler, anya to update kernel metadata schema, eli to add attach-time check. we'll reconvene in #eng-runtime in 45m for an initial signal check. :thumbsup:

sam: quick note — I dumped the KV page table after repro and saw a surprising duplicate reference causing the copy path. adding assertions in staging.
eli: nice catch. if that duplication is a separate bug we should still fix but keep selector guard anyway.

maya: ok closing for now, will post postmortem draft after the 2-hour observation window.
